purpose: Census how the 94 Korean banner occurrence rows reference already-prepared Banner/Picture_Notice display assets, without performing image hashing, visual duplicate detection, candidate matching, or final asset ownership modeling.

coreDecision.meaning: The current schedule stores the display-asset family and filename on each Korean occurrence row. This is an occurrence-level reference location, not proof that the occurrence owns the underlying asset or that the filename is a canonical asset identity.

Banner.observedUse: Current NEW and TRIPLE display behavior uses the larger Banner family under the existing schedule rules.

Picture_Notice.observedUse: Current SINGLE, DUAL, and WISH display behavior uses the Picture_Notice family under the existing schedule rules.

manualReplacementSemantics.rule: Do not interpret displayImageStatus=manual-replacement as displayImageFile missing. Most manual-replacement rows already reference a concrete replacement file.

visualTypeSemantics.importantBoundary: visualType records how the banner source/display case is characterized in the assembled schedule. It is not the same axis as displayImageType. Prefab-origin single-rerun rows can still reference a prepared Picture_Notice webp display asset.
visualTypeSemantics.prefabReferencePattern: Observed prefab rows reference Picture_Notice assets with matched status in the current schedule.
doNotInfer: Do not treat visualType=prefab as meaning there is no static website image.
Do not use visualType alone as canonical asset identity.

reuseDecision.observation: Multiple dated occurrences can carry the same displayImageFile reference when they reuse the same verified CardPool/banner source.
reuseDecision.importantLimit: The reverse is not safe: the same filename or apparent visual reuse must not be used by itself to prove two occurrences share a canonical banner definition.
reuseDecision.reason: Manual replacement assets can also be intentionally reused across multiple dated manual occurrences, and Stage 1 does not perform content hashing or visual equivalence analysis.
reuseDecision.relationRule: Source/recurrence identity comes from the verified relation layer first; asset references are supporting display evidence only.

directoryAndExistencePolicy.existingValidatorBehavior: For every non-null displayImageFile, scripts/validate_kr_schedule.cjs checks the corresponding Banner or Picture_Notice directory for the named file.
directoryAndExistencePolicy.reason: Stage 1-6 is a reference census. The project already has a schedule validator for file existence; this stage does not replace Stage 3 asset inventory/hash/diff work with another deep asset crawl.

prohibitedInferences: Do not promote displayImageFile into canonical bannerId or canonical assetId.
Do not infer CardPool/Hero/event relations from asset filename equality.
Do not infer canonical banner recurrence solely from the same image reference.
Do not classify manual-replacement as missing-image when a concrete replacement filename exists.
Do not hash or visually compare the asset collection in Stage 1-6.
Do not deduplicate or rename Banner/Picture_Notice files in Stage 1.
notDecided: Whether one canonical banner definition owns one or multiple display variants
Whether Banner and Picture_Notice are alternate renditions of the same source banner in each case

nextStartPoint.task: Representative fixture validation across the frozen Stage 1 findings
consume: Treat displayImageType/displayImageFile as occurrence-level display references, not canonical ownership.
Current population: Banner 37, Picture_Notice 57; matched 73, manual-replacement 21; non-null file 93, null 1; static 81, prefab 13.
Manual-replacement is a provenance/status distinction and usually still has a concrete replacement file.
Same verified source can reuse the same asset reference across multiple occurrence dates, but asset equality alone cannot establish source identity.
Defer hash/diff, visual duplicate grouping, and asset ownership to Stage 3.
